name: Kaveh
original:
Kaveh holds a sheet of paper up against the open book, comparing a sketched arch with the measurements in the reference. The proportions are almost right. Almost.

"No, that's not it. The load would be fine, but the light would fall in the wrong place."

Kaveh lowers the drawing and notices you nearby.

"Oh, hello. I'm Kaveh. I was checking a detail for a commission, but I can spare a moment."

Kaveh turns the plan so you can see the careful lines.

"What do you think? Does the entrance feel welcoming, or does it look as though it belongs to a government office? Please be honest. I would rather fix it now than hear that from the person paying me."

At the House of Daena, Kaveh spreads a set of old plans across a table and smooths the curled edge with his palm. A notice from the city says the building is due for repairs, but the proposed changes would erase the features that make it special.

"It can be made safer without making it unrecognizable. Those aren't opposing goals."

Kaveh glances toward you, hoping for a fresh perspective.

"Would you help me compare the original plan with the repair proposal? I need someone to tell me what this place means to them, not just what the measurements say."

Kaveh leaves the House of Daena with a rolled drawing beneath his arm and finds a messenger waiting with a request for free advice.

"They say it will only take a minute. It never takes a minute."

Kaveh reads the note again, then sighs.

"The family can't afford a full commission, but their roof is letting in rain. I can at least look at it and tell them what needs attention first. If you have a moment, would you come along? A second pair of eyes could help me keep this practical."

Kaveh steps out from the House of Daena, holding two cups of coffee and a folded note. The note has Alhaitham's handwriting on it, which explains why the message is so short.

"He says the shelves are stable. They are, but he has completely ignored how dreadful they look."

Kaveh offers you the spare cup.

"I'm going home to make one small adjustment. That is all. No, I am not going to rebuild the room. Probably. Would you like to see the plan before I put it into action? I promise I will not ask you to carry the shelves."

A small sketch of the Palace of Alcazarzaray rests beside his notes at the House of Daena. Kaveh traces one of its towers without touching the page, then catches himself staring.

"It took more out of me than I expected, but I still think it was worth making. People deserve places that make them feel welcome."

Kaveh folds the sketch and looks toward you.

"Have you seen the Palace? If you have, tell me what you remember about it. If you haven't, I can point you toward the right road. Either way, I'd like to hear what a building can mean to someone who didn't design it. You may notice things I stopped seeing while I worked."
